issues.claim: Delay the touch after your move, and it tickles again.
issues.problem: Sources (Sci Am, Blakemore robot studies) say a small delay can make it feel tickly, increasingly with longer delay; 'again' implies full restoration.
issues.fix: Delay the touch a little after your move, and it can feel ticklish again.

issues.claim: Your brain only mutes the touches it saw coming.
issues.problem: Rhetorical generalization; sources only describe attenuation of self-generated, predicted touch, so 'only' is stronger than the evidence.
issues.fix: Your brain mutes the touches it predicts, and lets the surprises through.

issues.claim: A stranger's touch has no prediction, so it still tickles.
issues.problem: Sci Am: cerebellum predicts own-movement sensations 'but not when someone else does'; 'stranger' is rhetorical (any other person), and Wikipedia says surprise is only 'thought' to be needed.
issues.fix: Someone else's touch can't be predicted this way, so it still tickles.
